1.explanation:
1. src/ol/renderer/canvas/ImageLayer.js  
   • This class is responsible for sizing and drawing the off‐screen canvas for image layers. It always uses frameState.pixelRatio to compute canvas.width/height and calls getRenderPixelSize(frameState.pixelRatio), ignoring the ImageWMS source’s configured ratio_ (which defaults to 1).  
2. src/ol/renderer/canvas/common.js  
   • The helper getRenderPixelSize() multiplies the world-extent dimensions by the passed‐in pixelRatio. Because ImageLayer.js always hands it the device pixelRatio, the canvas ends up oversized whenever source.ratio_ differs.  
3. src/ol/source/ImageWMS.js  
   • The WMS source exposes an optional ratio_ property (default 1) that should define the pixel ratio for requested images. Because the renderer never uses this ratio_, a 1× WMS image still gets drawn into a 2× (or higher) canvas on HiDPI screens, wasting memory. Adjusting ImageLayer.js to use source.ratio_ (or the image’s pixelRatio property) when sizing the canvas will eliminate the overallocation.
1.bug_scenario: When displaying an ImageWMS source on a HiDPI (high-pixel-ratio) device, OpenLayers always sizes the internal canvas using the device’s display pixel ratio (e.g. 2×), even if the WMS source was explicitly requested at a 1× pixel ratio. The result is a canvas that is twice as wide and tall as needed—using four times the GPU/JS memory—because the rendering code never falls back to the source’s own “ratio” parameter.

2.explanation: The file src/ol/renderer/canvas/ImageLayer.js is where the offscreen canvas for drawing the image layer is created and sized. It currently uses frameState.pixelRatio (the device/display pixel ratio) unconditionally when computing canvas.width/height and context.scale, rather than using the image source’s own pixelRatio (often 1 for WMS). As a result, on HiDPI screens the canvas is oversized and wastes memory. Correcting this to use image.getPixelRatio() when sizing and scaling the canvas will fix the over-allocation.
2.bug_scenario: On HiDPI (high pixel-density) displays, when rendering an ImageLayer (e.g. from a WMS source) whose own pixelRatio is 1, the renderer nonetheless uses the map’s display pixelRatio to size the offscreen canvas. This doubles the canvas’ width and height (for a devicePixelRatio of 2), and so uses 4× the memory needed. The bug images show normal WMS tiles loaded, but the allocated canvas is written out as twice the expected dimensions.
